description:
Found by s527a's §31 probe (2026-10-24).  With the vendored PPI `sub _ { ... }` is now a Statement::Sub named `_` (group H; t/op/filetest.t:161-162 moved DROP -> OK in the gate-SET scan and both rows print 1 as perl does).  But a CALL of that sub is still dropped:

    sub _ { "x" } print _(), "y\n";      # perl: xy
    PCL: statement dropped ... print _(), "\n"; -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ['Token::Magic<_>', ...]

PPI (master and branch alike) lexes the `_` of `_()` as Token::Magic, the stat filehandle -- it is the stat filehandle everywhere but after `sub`, and a `_` followed directly by `(` is a call in perl (`-f _` never takes parens).  Two possible fixes: (a) on the PPI branch, `_` followed by `(` is a Word (Token/Word.pm __underscore_class, the helper group H added: one more condition); (b) at PCL's lowering, a Magic `_` followed by a List is a call to `main::_`.  (a) is the right layer (a token class) and is a new row for s527b's tokenizer batch.  Reproducer: scratch/s527a/residual/filetest-sub_.pl in the s527a worktree.

=== DONE (s543f) ===
FIXED AT THE SOURCE: PCL's PPI group BG (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §73, branch pcl-s543f e0f5c8cc) -- Token/Word.pm's `__underscore_class` makes a lone `_` Magic (the stat filehandle) only after a filetest operator (`-e _`, `-f -w _`) and after `stat` / `lstat` with or without a `(`, a Word everywhere else, which is perl's rule (toke.c reads `_` as a plain word; op.c ck_ftst gives the bareword its meaning there).  `sub _ { "x" } print _(), "y"` prints xy; `_("a")`, `_ ("b")`, `sort _ LIST`, `Q->_()`, `(_ => 1)` + `$h{_}` + `@h{_, "a"}` all = perl.  The narrower first rule (`_(`, `=>`, `->`, `sort`) was measured and dropped: it made `(_ => 5)` right but left its reads `@h{_, "a"}` wrong.  PPI's fuzz fixture 45 (`_+...`) changed by exactly its first token (four conjuncts; `perl -MO=Deparse -e '_+1;'` prints `'_' + 1;`).  PCL needed no change.  Probe tables scratch/s543f/p3 (20 rows) main 13 -> tree 20 SAME, pu 3 -> 4 of 4.  Guards: Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t §73 rows (fail on main), registry row §73 (its `got` is 1.291's), twins §73.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-105 `8ef15927` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-22; s543f = PPI batch 11 merged; gate on merged main 380 files / 12,397 rows PASS) -- the guard row named in the DONE block above is in the gate; no baseline row is keyed on this task (the hits for the number in baselines/ are a row number, perl's own test label and a history comment).
